1	# sd 1.0.0 — stdio behavioral probe report
2	
3	Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`sd 1.0.0`). All probes were black-box: command-line, stdin/stdout/stderr, and files only.
4	All byte dumps are from `od -c`. Exit codes captured via `echo $?` / `PIPESTATUS`.
5	Note: the probing shell had `NO_COLOR=1` and `TERM=dumb` pre-set; tests that matter were repeated with those unset/overridden.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. stdin source variants
10	
11	### 1a. stdin closed (`</dev/null`)
12	```
13	$ /workspace/executable a b </dev/null
14	exit=0, stdout: (empty, 0 bytes), stderr: (empty)
15	```
16	
17	### 1b. empty pipe
18	```
19	$ printf '' | /workspace/executable a b
20	exit=0, stdout: (empty), stderr: (empty)
21	```
22	
23	### 1c. piped data
24	```
25	$ printf 'hello a world\n' | /workspace/executable a b
26	exit=0, stdout: h e l l o   b   w o r l d \n
27	```
28	
29	### 1d. redirected file (`sd a b < file`)
30	```
31	$ printf 'foo a bar\n' > in4.txt; /workspace/executable a b < in4.txt
32	exit=0, stdout: f o o   b   b a r \n
33	```
34	Identical transformation to in-place file mode (`sd a b file` produces the same bytes in the file).
35	
36	### 1e. stdin is a TTY
37	sd does **not** detect or special-case a tty; it reads stdin until EOF like any other source.
38	- Under `script -qec '/workspace/executable a b' /dev/null` with stdin from `/dev/null`: immediate EOF, exit=0, no output.
39	- With delayed input fed through the pty:
40	  ```
41	  $ (sleep 1; printf 'x a y\n'; sleep 0.5) | timeout 5 script -qec '/workspace/executable a b' /dev/null
42	  exit=0, captured pty output: x   a   y \r\n  x   b   y \r\n
43	  ```
44	  (first `x a y\r\n` is the pty's own echo; `x b y\r\n` is sd's output with the pty's `\n`→`\r\n` translation).
45	- With no input ever sent, sd blocks reading the tty (confirmed via 3 s wait; it only exited when the pty closed). **It would block forever on an interactive tty until Ctrl-D.**
46	
47	---
48	
49	## 2. Trailing-newline handling on stdout
50	
51	Output byte count exactly tracks the input — **no newline is ever added or removed**.
52	
53	```
54	$ printf 'no newline a' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
55	n o   n e w l i n e   b            (12 bytes, NO trailing \n), exit=0
56	$ printf 'with newline a\n' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
57	w i t h   n e w l i n e   b \n     (trailing \n preserved)
58	$ printf 'a' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
59	b                                    (1 byte)
60	```
61	
62	## 3. CRLF passthrough
63	
64	```
65	$ printf 'line1 a\r\nline2\r\n' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
66	l i n e 1   b \r\n l i n e 2 \r\n
67	```
68	CRLF preserved byte-for-byte. Note: `$` anchors are **not** CRLF-aware:
69	```
70	$ printf 'a\r\nb\r\n' | /workspace/executable 'a$' 'X' | od -c
71	a \r\n b \r\n        (unchanged — 'a$' does not match before \r\n)
72	```
73	
74	## 4. NUL bytes and invalid UTF-8
75	
76	Both are passed through untouched, exit=0, no error, no replacement char. Matching still works around them (the regex engine is byte-oriented but Unicode-aware).
77	
78	```
79	$ printf 'a\0b a c\n' | /workspace/executable a Z | od -c
80	Z \0 b   Z   c \n                          exit=0, stderr empty
81	$ printf 'x\0y\n' | /workspace/executable -F 'x' 'Q' | od -c
82	Q \0 y \n
83	$ printf 'good \xff\xfe a end\n' | /workspace/executable a Z | od -c
84	g o o d   377 376   Z   e n d \n           exit=0, stderr empty (same with -F)
85	$ printf 'p\x80q\n' | /workspace/executable p q | od -c
86	q 200 q \n
87	```
88	
89	Regex `.` over these bytes:
90	```
91	$ printf 'x\xffy\n' | /workspace/executable 'x.y' 'M' | od -c
92	x 377 y \n        (NO match — '.' does not match an invalid-UTF-8 byte)
93	$ printf 'x\0y\n' | /workspace/executable 'x.y' 'M' | od -c
94	M \n              (match — '.' DOES match NUL, a valid codepoint U+0000)
95	```
96	(Consistent with a `regex::bytes`-style engine with Unicode mode on.)
97	
98	## 5. Zero matches
99	
100	Output = input, byte-identical (including absence of trailing newline). Exit 0. stdout is still written.
101	
102	```
103	$ printf 'nothing here\n' | /workspace/executable zzz qqq | od -c
104	n o t h i n g   h e r e \n        exit=0
105	$ printf 'nothing here' | /workspace/executable zzz qqq | od -c
106	n o t h i n g   h e r e           (no trailing newline added)
107	$ printf '' | /workspace/executable zzz qqq | od -c
108	(empty)                             exit=0
109	```
110	
111	Zero-match **file** in-place: the file is still rewritten (mtime updated to now) even though content is unchanged:
112	```
113	$ touch -d '2020-01-01' z.txt; /workspace/executable zzz qqq z.txt
114	exit=0; mtime after: 2026-08-10 ...; content byte-identical
115	```
116	
117	## 6. Buffering / streaming model
118	
119	**sd reads ALL of stdin before writing ANY output.** It is not streaming.
120	
121	- Delayed-input test: `(printf 'first a\n'; sleep 2; printf 'second a\n') | sd a b | timestamp-each-line` — both output lines arrived at the same timestamp (~2 s in), i.e. after stdin EOF.
122	- 50 MB pipe: `cat big50.bin | sd a b > out` — 52,428,800 bytes in, 52,428,800 out, byte-identical to expected (every `a` replaced), exit 0, ~1.05 s wall.
123	- Peak RSS (polled `/proc/$pid/status` VmHWM) for the 50 MB run: **107,752 kB ≈ 105 MB** — about 2× the input size (full input buffer + full output buffer in memory).
124	- Consequence: infinite stdin (e.g. `yes`) never terminates — see §7.
125	
126	## 7. Broken pipe on stdout
127	
128	```
129	$ set -o pipefail; cat big50.bin | /workspace/executable a b | head -c 5
130	head got: b b c   b        (first 5 bytes)
131	PIPESTATUS = 0 1 0         (sd exit code = 1)
132	sd stderr (exact bytes): e r r o r :   B r o k e n   p i p e   ( o s   e r r o r   3 2 ) \n
133	```
134	i.e. the literal 33-byte line:
135	```
136	error: Broken pipe (os error 32)
137	```
138	Exit code on EPIPE = **1** (no panic, no 101). SIGPIPE is evidently ignored/handled (Rust default).
139	
140	With an **infinite** producer the consumer closing does not help, because sd never finishes reading stdin:
141	```
142	$ timeout 3 bash -c 'yes "match a" | /workspace/executable a b 2>/dev/null | head -c 5'
143	exit=124          (timed out — sd hangs reading stdin forever)
144	```
145	
146	Other write-side errors use the same format:
147	```
148	$ printf 'a\n' | /workspace/executable a b > /dev/full
149	exit=1, stderr: error: No space left on device (os error 28)\n
150	```
151	
152	## 8. Files AND stdin both given — precedence
153	
154	**File arguments win; stdin is ignored completely** (never read, never a fallback):
155	
156	```
157	$ printf 'file content a\n' > f1.txt
158	$ printf 'stdin content a\n' | /workspace/executable a b f1.txt
159	exit=0, stdout: (empty), stderr: (empty)
160	f1.txt afterwards: f i l e   c o n t e n t   b \n     (modified in place; stdin untouched)
161	```
162	Even with a nonexistent file there is no stdin fallback:
163	```
164	$ printf 'stdin a\n' | /workspace/executable a b /no/such
165	exit=1, stdout: (empty), stderr: error: invalid path: /no/such\n
166	```
167	A `-` argument is treated as a literal filename, not stdin:
168	```
169	$ printf 'a\n' | /workspace/executable a b -
170	exit=1, stderr: error: invalid path: -\n
171	```
172	
173	## 9. Error-message encoding on stderr
174	
175	All error messages are plain ASCII, no ANSI color/attributes — **even when stderr is a tty** (verified under `script`; only the pty's `\n`→`\r\n` translation appeared). Exact strings:
176	
177	- Invalid regex (exit 1):
178	  ```
179	  error: invalid regex parse error:
180	      (
181	      ^
182	  error: unclosed group
183	  ```
184	  Exact bytes: `error: invalid regex parse error:\n    (\n    ^\nerror: unclosed group\n`
185	- Nonexistent path (exit 1): `error: invalid path: /nonexistent/path.txt\n`
186	- Directory as file arg (exit 1): `error: No such device (os error 19)\n`
187	- Broken pipe (exit 1): `error: Broken pipe (os error 32)\n`
188	- /dev/full (exit 1): `error: No space left on device (os error 28)\n`
189	- Missing required CLI arg (exit **2**, clap usage error):
190	  ```
191	  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
192	    <REPLACE_WITH>
193	
194	  Usage: executable <FIND> <REPLACE_WITH> [FILES]...
195	
196	  For more information, try '--help'.
197	  ```
198	
199	Exit-code summary: 0 = success (including zero matches, empty input); 1 = runtime errors (regex compile, I/O, invalid path, broken pipe); 2 = CLI usage errors; 101 = panic (documented in man page; not triggered by any probe here — e.g. an out-of-range capture ref `'(a)' → '$2'` did NOT panic, it replaced with the empty string: `printf 'a\n' | sd '(a)' '$2'` → `\n`, exit 0).
200	
201	## 10. Environment variables / preview colors
202	
203	Preview mode (`-p`) writes the full would-be-new content to stdout and leaves the file untouched. **No ANSI color codes are emitted in any configuration tested**, and no env var had any observable effect on output bytes:
204	
205	| Configuration | Output bytes |
206	|---|---|
207	| `-p`, stdout=pipe | plain text, no escapes |
208	| `-p`, stdout=tty (`script`) | plain text, no escapes |
209	| `-p`, tty, `NO_COLOR` unset, `TERM=xterm-256color` | identical plain text |
210	| `-p`, tty, `TERM=dumb` | identical plain text |
211	| `-p`, pipe, `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` | identical plain text |
212	| `-p`, pipe, `NO_COLOR=1` (default env) | identical plain text |
213	
214	```
215	$ script -qec 'env -u NO_COLOR TERM=xterm-256color /workspace/executable -p a b pv.txt' /dev/null | od -c
216	b l p h b   b   o m e g b \r\n s e c o n d   l i n e   b \r\n     (no ESC bytes anywhere)
217	```
218	So for reimplementation: preview output = transformed content, colors never appear; `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `COLORTERM` are all inert. (`-p` with stdin behaves the same as normal stdin→stdout mode.)
219	
220	## 11. Misc stdio-adjacent findings
221	
222	- Empty pattern: `printf 'ab\n' | sd '' 'X'` → `X a X b X \n X` (6 bytes `XaXbX\nX`) — empty regex matches at every position including after the final `\n`; exit 0.
223	- `--` end-of-flags works with stdin: `printf 'foo -w\n' | sd -- '-w' 'X'` → `foo X\n`.
224	- sd replaces **all** occurrences (default `-n 0` = unlimited), including inside words: `abc a def` → `bbc b def` with `sd a b`.
225	- stdout writes happen only after full stdin EOF, then the complete transformed buffer is written (single-pass, not chunked per line).
226

228	
229	## 10-line summary — most important/surprising findings
230	
231	1. sd reads ALL of stdin into memory before writing a single byte — with `yes` it hangs forever even after the consumer closes the pipe (timeout 124).
232	2. Memory footprint ≈ 2× input size (50 MB input → ~105 MB peak RSS); output written in one shot after EOF.
233	3. Broken pipe: exit code 1 with exact stderr line `error: Broken pipe (os error 32)\n` — no panic, no SIGPIPE death.
234	4. Byte-exact passthrough: never adds/removes a trailing newline; CRLF preserved verbatim; NUL and invalid UTF-8 (`\xff`, `\x80`) pass through untouched with exit 0.
235	5. Regex `.` matches NUL but NOT invalid-UTF-8 bytes (byte-oriented, Unicode-aware engine).
236	6. Zero matches still write full output (stdin mode) and still rewrite the file (mtime bumps) in file mode — exit 0 either way.
237	7. File args completely override stdin: piped stdin is silently ignored when files are given, even if the file doesn't exist; `-` is a literal filename, not stdin.
238	8. TTY stdin is not detected at all — sd blocks reading until EOF (Ctrl-D), same as a pipe.
239	9. Error messages are plain ASCII with no ANSI color even on a tty; exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime/IO/regex errors, 2 clap usage errors; `$2`-style out-of-range group refs yield empty string, not a panic.
240	10. `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` have zero observable effect — preview mode (`-p`) never emits ANSI colors; it just prints the transformed content to stdout without modifying the file.
